Evidence: Gate re-exports 16 values incl. allocateEventSeq, appendEventRecord, listEventRowsNewestFirst, EPHEMERAL_EVENT_TYPES, resolveEvent*, DEFAULT/MAX_EVENT_PAGE_LIMIT; only eventsGate.* (6 ports) + 2 reset helpers are used outside (create-app.ts:365, routes/events.ts:39, tests)
Reproduction: grep importers of events/* outside domain: only create-app.ts and routes/events.ts use the gate object
Root: Facade was written as a re-export barrel of the whole module, not "export only what outsiders use" (AGENTS.md §2)
Impact: Contract surface wider than consumers need; internal refactors become breaking changes
Fix: Trim gate exports to ports + types actually consumed; keep test-only resets; move allocator/record/rows exports out of the gate (or re-export under a clearly test-only name)
Tests: Gate-shape test asserting exported names == allowed list

Evidence: const workspaceId = resolveEventWorkspaceId(event.payload) ?? (await workspaceOfChannel(channelId)); resolveEventWorkspaceId reads payload.workspaceId verbatim (event-classification.ts:45-48)
Reproduction: Call eventsGate.record({type:"message:new",channelId:"ch-of-ws-A",payload:{channelId:"ch-of-ws-A",workspaceId:"ws-B"}}); line lands in ws-B folder while the channel row belongs to ws-A
Root: Write scope trusts a producer-supplied field before the authoritative channel->workspace lookup
Impact: A buggy/malicious producer can write (and later read) channel history into another workspace's folder; splits the log from the channel's true scope
Fix: Resolve scope from the channel row first; treat payload.workspaceId as a cross-check/audit field only (or reject mismatch); the spec calls workspaceId "an audit field, not an enforcement field" (Events.md Gaps) but the writer uses it for routing
Tests: events-log.test.ts: add a case asserting channel-row scope wins over a conflicting payload workspaceId

Evidence: route calls eventsGate.listRecent(channelId,{afterSeq,limit}) with no workspaceId arg; no request.workspaceId use anywhere in the route; store resolves scope from the channel
Reproduction: Start server, inject GET /api/events/recent?channelId=<id-of-other-workspace> from loopback: 200 with that channel's events
Root: Reads are not tenant-asserted at the HTTP boundary; tenant scope is derived from the channel id only
Impact: In loopback/desktop single-user model this is acceptable; in any multi-workspace deployment with remote callers (or a future non-loopback trust change) any channel id grants read of its history
Fix: Thread request.workspaceId (x-workspace-id) into the route and compare with the channel's resolved workspace; 403/404 on mismatch; or document the loopback-only trust explicitly in the route

Evidence: channelWorkspaceMemo caches only non-null hits; cleared wholesale at >5000 entries (:60); no per-entry TTL/invalidation
Reproduction: Two workspaces both contain a channel row with the same id (or a channel row is created after a null resolution then copied), then call record twice
Root: Positive-only memo with no invalidation: the first resolved workspace is pinned for the process
Impact: Wrong workspace routing for a channel id that ever legitimately changes owner (rename/restore/migration); cross-tenant misroute compounding EVT-02
Fix: Key the memo by (workspaceId? no) or invalidate on workspace/channel mutations; at minimum document + expose a reset for ops
Tests: Unit test with a changed channel row between calls expecting the new owner

Evidence: listEventTail reads ALL rows (readEventRows -> readEventJsonl -> readFile), scans for head, pushes tail, sorts; no retention (Events.md Decisions)
Reproduction: Write 100k events to one channel; call GET /api/events/recent?channelId=..&afterSeq=<head-1>; measure latency/read bytes
Root: O(n) full-file read + sort per poll; log unbounded by design
Impact: Every client reconnect/gap-fetch pays full-file cost; memory spike on big logs; poll loops amplify
Fix: Tail-read from file end (reverse scan) or maintain an index; add retention/size bound decision (documented gap)
Tests: Perf test with a large synthetic file asserting bounded read (or a benchmark harness)

Evidence: flooredChannels memo: floor runs once per channel+workspace per process; a later counter reset (backup restore, manual copy, fresh workspace over existing events/) is not re-floored
Reproduction: Process A: record events 1..3 (floor memo set). Replace event-sequences.json with {"ch":0} on disk. Record again -> allocateEventSeq returns 1 (duplicate seq) without re-reading head
Root: Floor is memoized per process, not validated per allocation
Impact: Duplicate seq values in one log; afterSeq semantics degrade (a client that saw seq 3 will not re-see the re-issued 1..3) — replay silently skips re-issued rows
Fix: Re-floor when counter value < file head at allocation time (cheap guard: compare counter to last known head) or key the memo to counter file mtime
Tests: Unit test: reset the counter file mid-process and assert seq continues past head

Evidence: withFileLock chains promises per key; single-process only (header comment: multi-process writers need PG)
Reproduction: Run two Node processes appending to the same channel log; observe interleaved/duplicate seq
Root: In-process mutex only; multi-process (api+worker) unsupported by design
Impact: BullMQ multi-process mode would corrupt seq/order if a second writer were ever wired (documented; worker hook deliberately not wired)
Fix: Keep the single-writer constraint; if worker logging is ever needed, add a cross-process lock or real store first (spec already says this)
Tests: None (documented constraint); guard test that worker.ts contains no events hook

Reproduction: Emit events while an append fails; GET /api/metrics; counters absent

Evidence: catch -> stats.failed++, console.warn, return null; no retry, no outbox, no dead-letter
Reproduction: Make the events dir unwritable (test already simulates via ENOTDIR blocker); emit; event is lost; client gap-fetch can never recover it
Root: Best-effort local append with no recovery path
Impact: Silent history loss for the duration of the failure; replay reports a hole (honest but unrecoverable server-side)
Fix: Add a bounded retry/queue or document the accepted loss with an operator-visible signal (metric + threshold alert)
Tests: Existing failed-append test covers the swallow; add a retry test once implemented

Impact: Debt: if those internals move, the test breaks in a way the gate script flags only as a warning
Fix: Route the imports through agent-gate / runtime-gate when touching the file

Evidence: No unique constraint / seen-set on eventId; spec Gaps: "No dedupe on append"
Reproduction: Call eventsGate.record twice with the same eventId; two lines, seqs n and n+1

Impact: Latent duplicate history if any producer ever retries an emit
Fix: Add an eventId dedupe window (bounded LRU or per-channel seen set) only if re-emission is introduced; document as accepted today

Evidence: Route response omits headSeq and workspaceId; store returns headSeq
Reproduction: GET /api/events/recent returns exactly {channelId, events, lastSeq} (route test asserts key set)
Root: Route intentionally narrows the store result to the client contract
Impact: Server-side consumers of headSeq must call the gate directly; no bug, but headSeq is dead weight on the public route path
Fix: Keep as-is (client contract) or expose headSeq additively if a consumer needs it
Tests: Route test already pins the shape

Evidence: safeChannelFileId collapses [^A-Za-z0-9_-] to "_" for the FILE, but allocateEventSeq keys the counter by RAW channelId (obj[channelId]) and listEventTail does not filter rows by row.channelId
Reproduction: Record to channelId "a/b" and "a?b": both append to a_b.jsonl with independent counters both starting at 1 (duplicate seqs in one file); GET recent for "a/b" returns BOTH channels' rows
Root: Lossy filename sanitization + per-raw-id counters + reader trusting the file as channel-scoped
Impact: Cross-channel bleed AND duplicate seq values for colliding ids; afterSeq cursor semantics degrade on the shared file
Fix: Include the raw channelId in the record and filter on read, or hash the id to a collision-resistant filename (and key counters by the same canonical id)
Tests: Unit test: two colliding ids must not see each other's rows nor share a seq space

Evidence: recordBrokerEvent never validates event.type against BrokerEventMap at runtime; payload passed through verbatim
Reproduction: eventsGate.record({eventId:"x",type:"unknown:type" as never,channelId:"c",payload:{}}); line written with unknown type
Root: Runtime trust in the producer's typing; no validation at the append boundary
Impact: A typo'd producer type becomes durable history and replays to clients that may not know it; downstream reducers must tolerate unknown keys
Fix: Validate type against a runtime key set (or at least classify unknown keys) at the append boundary
Tests: Unit test: unknown type is rejected or explicitly allowed by policy
